source: Earthdawn 4E Player's Guide — the Weapons, Armor & Shields, Magical Equipment, and Adventuring Equipment tables (Weapons p.406-410; Armor and Shields p.411-415; Magical Equipment p.415-423; Adventuring Equipment p.423-426; tables on pp.433-439). The reference CATALOG: each entry's mechanics live in an `effects` array in the controlled taxonomy vocabulary, so the engine gathers them exactly as it does racial/discipline effects. A character owns items by name (data/character.json `items: [{ name, equipped }]`) — the numbers are reference, not per-character input.

notes.armor: Worn armor confers Physical/Mystic Armor (damage reducers) via `armor-modifier` effects, and its Initiative penalty via a `characteristic-modifier` on Initiative (measure: step). `living` marks elemental 'living' armor (the only kind an obsidiman may wear atop Natural Armor; PG p.48). `ref` holds display-only stats (cost/weight/availability).
notes.shield: Shields do NOT add to Armor — they raise Physical/Mystic DEFENSE (`defense-modifier`) and carry an Initiative penalty. `shatterThreshold` is display-only reference.
notes.weapon: Weapons carry an `attack-modifier` on the attack's Damage step (target `attack`/`Damage`, `operation: add`, measure: step). Every category — melee, missile, and thrown — adds its Damage Step to the Strength-step base (EFFECT-TAXONOMY v3 §4.1; the base is the engine default, not stored here). STR/DEX minima, size, ranges, and entangle details are display-only in `ref`. Ammo rows from the missile table are separate `ammunition` entries.
notes.blood-charm: Blood charms are activated items: their bonuses are `situational` typed effects (with `scope`), the one-time implant Blood Magic Damage is a `note` and is also captured as numeric `characteristic-modifier` effects (operation: subtract, measure: rating, `condition`: situational, `scope`: implanted) on the Death and Unconsciousness ratings, and the Alchemy crafting difficulty (the rulebook's EDN) is display-only in `ref` as `craftingDifficultyNumber`.
notes.healing-aid: Healing aids grant one-shot bonuses encoded as `situational` test modifiers; `craftingDifficultyNumber` (the Alchemy crafting difficulty, the rulebook's EDN) is display-only in `ref`.
notes.magic-item: Common magic items: numeric, always-relevant mechanics are typed effects; one-shot, non-numeric, or activated properties are `note` effects.
notes.gear: Adventuring gear is mostly display-only (`effects: []`); kits record their contents in a `note`, and items with a specific game rule (e.g. Healing Kit +1 Recovery, chain/rope break tests) carry that rule as an effect.
notes.presentation: PRESENTATION LAYER ONLY. Optional `presentation` object holds display strings for the UI and is never read by the engine — it carries no game mechanics. `shortEffect` is a 3-4 word label shown in the Equipment tile's right-hand space for note-type items; the authoritative rule always lives in `effects` (and its full `summary`). Items with a numeric effect derive their tile label in the view instead, so they carry no `shortEffect`.

A simple wooden flute.
A horn for music or signalling.
A stringed lute for a travelling musician.
A small whistle for tunes or signals.
Charts for plotting a course by land or water.

effects.summary: Map and scroll case with a basic star chart; required to use the Navigation talent.

ref.description: A flask of lamp oil, also useful as a firebomb.

effects.summary: Holds enough oil to fuel a lantern for eight hours.

ref.description: A sheet of paper or parchment for writing.
Surgical tools and supplies for a physician, good for three uses.

effects.summary: Required to use the Physician skill; can be used three times before its consumable supplies are exhausted.

ref.description: A refill of a physician's supplies, good for three uses.

effects.summary: Refill of three applications for a physician's kit; requires the tools from the basic kit to be useful.

ref.description: A trimmed feather pen for writing.
A leather case holding about forty arrows or thirty bolts.

effects.summary: Typical quiver holds 40 arrows or 30 bolts.

ref.description: Strong rope, sold by the yard.

effects.summary: Binding/climbing rope; a bound character breaks free with a successful Strength (8) test.

ref.description: A plain cloth sack for hauling goods.

effects.summary: Holds approximately 30 pounds of goods.

ref.description: A canvas tent for shelter on the road.
Lockpicks and fine tools for defeating locks and traps.

effects.summary: Required to use the Lock Picking skill.

ref.description: A pitch-soaked torch for light.

effects.summary: Illuminates a 10-yard radius; unlit may be used as an improvised club; a lit torch may set flammable targets alight.

ref.description: A skin holding about a day's water or wine.

effects.summary: A typical skin holds enough water for one day (the weight shown is for a full skin).

ref.description: A stone for keeping a blade's edge keen.
A vial of writing ink.

effects.summary: Each vial holds enough ink for eight to ten pages.

ref.description: Pen, ink, and paper for writing on the road.

effects.summary: Quill pen, writing ink, 10 sheets of parchment or paper, 2 candles, and 10 pieces of chalk.
